Q189872.lead: Bellerophon or Bellerophontes or Hipponous (Ancient Greek: Ἱππόνοος, lit. 'horse-knower'), was a divine Corinthian hero of Greek mythology, the son of Poseidon and Eurynome, and the foster son of Glaukos. He was "the greatest hero and slayer of monsters, alongside Cadmus and Perseus, before the days of Heracles".

Q190323.label: Atalanta
Q190323.description: Greek mythological character, the only female Argonaut
Q190323.lead: Atalanta is a heroine in Greek mythology. There are two versions of the huntress Atalanta: one from Arcadia, whose parents were Iasus and Clymene and who is primarily known from the tales of the Calydonian boar hunt and the Argonauts; and the other from Boeotia, who is the daughter of King Schoeneus and is primarily noted for her skill in the footrace.

Q190543.label: Alkmene
Q190543.lead: In Greek mythology, Alcmene or Alcmena ( alk-MEE-nə; Doric Greek: Ἀλκμάνα, romanized: Alkmána; Latin: Alcumena; meaning "strong in wrath") was the wife of Amphitryon, by whom she bore two children, Iphicles and Laonome. She is best known as the mother of Heracles, whose father was the god Zeus.

Q190563.label: Pontus
Q190563.lead: In Greek mythology, Pontus is the personification of the sea. In Hesiod's Theogony (8th or 7th century BC), he is the offspring of Gaia (the Earth), who produces him alone.

Q190565.label: Metis
Q190565.description: Oceanid of Greek mythology, goddess of wisdom, daughter of Oceanid and Tethys
Q190565.lead: Metis, in ancient Greek religion and mythology, was the pre-Olympian goddess of wisdom, counsel and deep thought, and a member of the Oceanids. She is notable for being the advisor and first wife of Zeus, the king of the gods.

Q191192.label: Giants
Q191192.lead: In Greek and Roman mythology, the Giants, also called Gigantes, were a race of great strength and aggression, though not necessarily of great size, known for the Gigantomachy (also spelled Gigantomachia), their battle with the Olympian gods. According to Hesiod, the Giants were the offspring of Gaia (Earth), born from the blood that fell when Uranus (Sky) was castrated by his Titan son Cronus.

Q191725.label: Aegeus
Q191725.lead: Aegeus was one of the kings of Athens in Greek mythology, who gave his name to the Aegean Sea, was the father of Theseus, and founded Athenian institutions.

Q192107.label: Hemera
Q192107.description: ancient Greek goddess of the day
Q192107.lead: In Greek mythology, Hemera was the personification of day. According to Hesiod, she was the daughter of Erebus (Darkness) and Nyx (Night), and the sister of Aether.

Q192109.label: Admetus
Q192109.description: king of Pherae in Thessaly, in Greek mythology
Q192109.lead: In Greek mythology, Admetus was a king of Pherae in Thessaly.

Q192136.label: Kreios
Q192136.description: Titan in Greek mythology, name that means ram
Q192136.lead: In Greek mythology, Crius, Krios or Kreios was one of the Titans, the children of Uranus (Sky) and Gaia (Earth).

Q192407.label: Orestes
Q192407.description: son of Agamemnon in Greek mythology
Q192407.lead: In Greek mythology, Orestes or Orestis was the son of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, and the brother of Electra and Iphigenia. He was also known by the patronymic Agamemnonides (Ἀγαμεμνονίδης), meaning "son of Agamemnon." He is the subject of multiple Ancient Greek plays (including Aeschylus' Oresteia), which depict his revenge, madness, and ritual purification.

Q192469.label: Atreus
Q192469.description: king of Mycenae, father of Agamemnon
Q192469.lead: In Greek mythology, Atreus was a king of Mycenae in the Peloponnese, the son of Pelops and Hippodamia, and the father of Agamemnon and Menelaus. His descendants became known collectively as the Atreidae (Ancient Greek: Ἀτρείδαι Atreidai).

Q192482.label: Telemachus
Q192482.description: in Greek mythology, the son of Odysseus and Penelope, a character from Homer's "Odyssey"
Q192482.lead: Telemachus is the son of Odysseus and Penelope in Greek mythology, and a central character in Homer's Odyssey. When Telemachus reached manhood, he visited Pylos and Sparta in search of his wandering father.

Q192638.label: Apollonius of Rhodes
Q192638.lead: Apollonius of Rhodes was an ancient Greek author, best known for the Argonautica, an epic poem about Jason and the Argonauts and their quest for the Golden Fleece.

Q192946.label: Tyndareus
Q192946.lead: In Greek mythology, Tyndareus was a Spartan king.

Q193115.label: Scylla
Q193115.description: nymph transformed into a sea monster by Circe in Greek mythology
Q193115.lead: In Greek mythology, Scylla is a legendary, man-eating monster that lives on one side of a narrow channel of water, opposite her counterpart, the sea-swallowing monster Charybdis. The two sides of the strait are within an arrow's range of each other—so close that sailors attempting to avoid the whirlpools of Charybdis would pass dangerously close to Scylla and vice versa.

Q193267.label: Nestor
Q193267.description: wise ruler of Pylos in Greek mythology, son of Neleus
Q193267.lead: In Greek mythology, Nestor of Gerenia was a legendary king of Pylos. He is a prominent secondary character in Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, where he appears as an elderly warrior who frequently offers advice to the other characters.

Q193609.label: Rhadamanthus
Q193609.description: Greek mythology character, son of Zeus and Europa
Q193609.lead: In Greek mythology, Rhadamanthus or Rhadamanthys was a wise king of Crete. As the son of Zeus and Europa he was considered a demigod.

Q19376.label: Andromache
Q19376.description: wife of Hector in Greek mythology
Q19376.lead: In Greek mythology, Andromache was the wife of Hector, daughter of Eetion, and sister to Podes. She was born and raised in the city of Cilician Thebe, over which her father ruled.

Q1956583.label: Mycene
Q1956583.description: daughter of Inachus in Greek mythology
Q1956583.lead: In Greek mythology, Mycene, was a daughter of Inachus, king of Argos and wife of Arestor. Mycene was said to be the eponym of Mycenae.

Q1968413.label: Mecisteus
Q1968413.description: son of Talaus and Lysimache in ancient Greek mythology
Q1968413.lead: In Greek mythology, Mecisteus was the son of Talaus and Lysimache. He was the father of Euryalus by Astyoche.

Q196865.label: Zethos
Q196865.lead: Amphion and Zethus (Ancient Greek: Ζῆθος, romanized: Zêthos) were, in ancient Greek mythology, the twin sons of Zeus (or Theobus) by Antiope. They are important characters in one of the two founding myths of the city of Thebes, because they constructed the city's walls.

Q199438.label: Nemean lion
Q199438.lead: The Nemean lion was a mythical lion in Greek mythology that lived at Nemea. It is most famous for being one of the mythical beasts killed by Heracles (Hercules) in his 12 labours.

Q199923.label: Dione
Q199923.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Dione is an oracular goddess and Titaness. She is primarily known from Book V of Homer's Iliad, where she tends to the wounds suffered by her daughter Aphrodite.

Q2001055.label: Diocles
Q2001055.lead: Diocles of Megara was an ancient Greek warrior from Athens who died a hero in Megara.

Q200382.label: Phorcys
Q200382.lead: In Greek mythology, Phorcys or Phorcus is a primordial sea god, generally cited (first in Hesiod) as the son of Pontus and Gaia (Earth). Classical scholar Karl Kerenyi conflated Phorcys with the similar sea gods Nereus and Proteus.

Q201411.label: Horae
Q201411.description: goddesses of the seasons and the natural portions of time in Greek mythology
Q201411.lead: In Greek mythology, the Horae, Horai or Hours were the goddesses of the seasons and the natural portions of time.

Q203673.label: Callisto
Q203673.lead: In Greek mythology, Callisto was a nymph (an Arcadian mountain nymph; an Oread), or the daughter of King Lycaon; the myth varies in such details. She was believed to be one of the followers of Artemis (Diana for the Romans) who was pursued by Zeus.

Q205233.label: Maia
Q205233.lead: In ancient Greek mythology, Maia, also spelled Maie, is one of the Pleiades and the mother of the messenger god Hermes by Zeus. Maia was identified with the Roman earth goddess Maia, the mother of Mercury.

Q205251.label: Plutus
Q205251.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Plutus is the god and the personification of wealth, and the son of the goddess of agriculture Demeter and the mortal Iasion.

Q206187.label: Aeacus
Q206187.description: son of Zeus in Greek mythology
Q206187.lead: Aeacus was a king of the island of Aegina in Greek mythology. He was a son of Zeus and the nymph Aegina, and the father of the heroes Peleus and Telamon.

Q206214.label: Amphitryon
Q206214.description: figure in Greek mythology, husband of Alcmene
Q206214.lead: Amphitryon, in Greek mythology, was a son of Alcaeus, king of Tiryns in Argolis. His mother was named either Astydameia, the daughter of Pelops and Hippodamia, or Laonome, daughter of Guneus, or else Hipponome, daughter of Menoeceus.

Q207273.label: Hyacinth
Q207273.lead: Hyacinth or Hyacinthus is a deified hero and a lover of Apollo in Greek mythology. His cult at Amyclae southwest of Sparta dates from the Mycenaean era.

Q207368.label: Echo
Q207368.lead: In Greek mythology, Echo was an Oread who resided on Mount Cithaeron. Zeus loved consorting with beautiful nymphs and often visited them on Earth.

Q207681.label: Cassiopeia
Q207681.description: figure in Greek mythology; queen of Aethiopia and wife of king Cepheus
Q207681.lead: Cassiopeia, also variously spelled as Cassiope (Ancient Greek: Κασσιόπη, romanized: Kassiópē) or Cassiepeia (Ancient Greek: Κασσιέπεια, romanized: Kassiépeia), is a figure in Greek and Roman mythology, the queen of Aethiopia and wife of King Cepheus. She was arrogant and vain, characteristics that led to the endangerment of her daughter Andromeda and her own downfall.

Q207715.label: Deucalion
Q207715.description: son of Prometheus in Greek mythology
Q207715.lead: In Greek mythology, Deucalion was the son of Prometheus; ancient sources name his mother as Clymene, Hesione, or Pronoia. He is closely connected with a flood myth in Greek mythology.

Q208017.label: Acrisius
Q208017.lead: In Greek mythology, Acrisius was a king of Argos. He was the grandfather of the famous Greek demi-god Perseus through his only daughter Danaë.

Q208256.label: Diomedes
Q208256.description: hero son of Tydeus in Greek mythology, king of Argos
Q208256.lead: Diomedes or Diomede is a hero in Greek mythology, known for his participation in the Trojan War. He was born to Tydeus and Deipyle and later became King of Argos, succeeding his maternal grandfather, Adrastus.

Q2084760.label: Phalereus
Q2084760.description: son of Icarius of Sparta in Greek mythology

Q209489.label: Ceto
Q209489.lead: Ceto is a primordial sea goddess in Greek mythology, the daughter of Pontus and his mother, Gaia. As a mythological figure, she is considered to be one of the most ancient deities, and bore a host of monstrous children fathered by Phorcys, another child of Gaia and Pontus.

Q210883.label: Danaus
Q210883.lead: In Greek mythology, Danaus was the king of Libya. His myth is a foundation legend of Argos, one of the foremost Mycenaean cities of the Peloponnesus.

Q211953.label: Anchises
Q211953.description: father of Aeneas in Greek mythology, lover of Aphrodite
Q211953.lead: In Greek and Roman mythology, Anchises was a member of the royal family of Troy. He was said to have been the son of King Capys of Dardania and Themiste, daughter of Ilus, who was son of Tros.

Q212087.label: Eurystheus
Q212087.description: king of Mycenae in Greek mythology
Q212087.lead: In Greek mythology, Eurystheus was king of Tiryns, one of three Mycenaean strongholds in the Argolid, although other authors including Homer and Euripides cast him as ruler of Argos.

Q212091.label: Aegisthus
Q212091.description: son of Thyestes in Greek mythology
Q212091.lead: Aegisthus was a figure in Greek mythology. Aegisthus is known from two primary sources: the first is Homer's Odyssey, believed to have been first written down by Homer at the end of the 8th century BC, and the second from Aeschylus's Oresteia, written in the 5th century BC. Aegisthus also features heavily in the action of Euripides's Electra (c.

Q212827.label: Philoctetes
Q212827.lead: Philoctetes or Philocthetes, according to Greek mythology, was the son of Poeas, king of Meliboea in Thessaly, and Demonassa or Methone. He was a Greek hero, famed as an archer, and a participant in the Trojan War.

Q213440.label: Tyche
Q213440.lead: Tyche was the presiding tutelary deity who governed the fortune and prosperity of a city, its destiny. In Classical Greek mythology, she is the daughter of the Titans Tethys and Oceanus, and she brings positive messages to people relating to external events outside their control.

Q213621.label: Niobe
Q213621.lead: Niobe was in Greek mythology a daughter of Tantalus and of either Dione or of Eurythemista or Euryanassa. She was the wife of Amphion and the sister of Pelops and Broteas.

Q21567935.label: Pierus
Q21567935.description: king of Emathia, father of the Pierides, eponym of Pieria
Q21567935.lead: In Greek mythology, Pierus was the king of Emathia in Macedonia. He was the eponym of Pieria and Mt.

Q223152.label: Adrastus
Q223152.lead: In Greek mythology, Adrastus or Adrestus was a king of Argos, and leader of the Seven against Thebes. He was the son of the Argive king Talaus, but was forced out of Argos by his dynastic rival Amphiaraus.

Q223690.label: Ino
Q223690.lead: In Greek mythology, Ino was a Theban princess who later became a queen of Boeotia. After her death and transfiguration, she was worshiped as a goddess under her epithet Leucothea, the "white goddess." Alcman called her "Queen of the Sea" (Ancient Greek: θαλασσομέδουσα, romanized: thalassomédousa), which, if not hyperbole, would make her a goddess parallel to Amphitrite.

Q23162.label: Asterios
Q23162.description: King of Crete and husband of Europa
Q23162.lead: In Greek mythology, Asterion or Asterius (Ἀστέριος) was a King of Crete and the foster-father of Minos.

Q23168.label: Minos
Q23168.description: Greek mythology character, son of Zeus and Europa, king of Crete
Q23168.lead: In Greek mythology, Minos was a king of Crete, son of Zeus and Europa. Every nine years, he made King Aegeus pick seven young boys and seven young girls to be sent to Daedalus's creation, the labyrinth, to be eaten by the Minotaur.

Q2316900.label: Leucippus
Q2316900.description: son of Perieres and father of the Leucippides
Q2316900.lead: In Greek mythology, Leucippus was a Messenian prince. The Boeotian town of Leuctra is said to have derived its name from him.

Q232128.label: Artemisia I of Caria
Q232128.description: 5th century BC queen of Halicarnassus, Kos, Nisyros and Kalymnos
Q232128.lead: Artemisia I of Caria (Ancient Greek: Ἀρτεμισία, transl. Ártemisía; fl.

Q237224.label: Bia
Q237224.description: ancient Greek goddess, personification of force and compulsion
Q237224.lead: In Greek mythology, Bia is the personification of violence.

Q2391785.label: Rhodope
Q2391785.description: daughter of Hebrus in Greek mythology
Q2391785.lead: In ancient Greek and Roman mythology, Rhodope is the wife of Haemus and queen of Thrace. She and her husband were punished together by being transformed into mountain ranges after daring to compare themselves to Zeus and Hera, the highest gods.

Q241971.label: Aeëtes
Q241971.description: son of Helios in Greek mythology
Q241971.lead: Aeëtes, or Aeeta, was the ruler of the eponymous realm of Aea in Greek mythology, a wondrous realm which from the fifth century B.C.E. onward became identified with the kingdom of Colchis east in the Black Sea. The name comes from the ancient Greek word αἰετός (aietós, "eagle").

Q242835.label: Amphion
Q242835.description: mythical musician and ruler at Thebes
Q242835.lead: Amphion and Zethus (Ancient Greek: Ζῆθος, romanized: Zêthos) were, in ancient Greek mythology, the twin sons of Zeus (or Theobus) by Antiope. They are important characters in one of the two founding myths of the city of Thebes, because they constructed the city's walls.

Q244318.label: Briseis
Q244318.description: daughter of Briseus in Greek mythology
Q244318.lead: Briseis, also known as Hippodameia (Ἱπποδάμεια, [hippodámeːa]), is a significant character in the Iliad. Her role as a status symbol is at the heart of the dispute between Achilles and Agamemnon that initiates the plot of Homer's epic.

Q2446699.label: Rhacius
Q2446699.description: cretan son of Lebes who settled in Caria
Q2446699.lead: In Greek mythology, Rhacius was the Cretan son of Lebes, who led a group of Greek settlers to Colophon in Asia Minor. With his wife Manto, daughter of the seer Tiresias, he became the father of Mopsus, a renowned seer.

Q2470563.label: Cedalion
Q2470563.lead: In Greek mythology, Cedalion was a servant of Hephaestus in Lemnos, an island in the Aegean Sea. Cedalion is best known for his part in aiding the hunter Orion navigate the world after being blinded, and helping him to reach Helios who healed his eyesight.

Q247617.label: Curetes
Q247617.description: minor Minoan and Greek deities, servants of Rhea

Q2479189.label: Ischys
Q2479189.description: son of Elatus and lover of Coronis in Greek mythology
Q2479189.lead: In Greek mythology, Ischys was the son of Elatus.

Q2495582.label: Phaeno
Q2495582.lead: In Greek mythology, Phaeno was one of the 3,000 Oceanids, water-nymph daughters of the Titans Oceanus and his sister-spouse Tethys.

Q250506.label: Tydeus
Q250506.description: son of Oeneus in Greek mythology
Q250506.lead: Tydeus was an Aetolian hero in Greek mythology, belonging to the generation before the Trojan War. He was one of the Seven against Thebes, and the father of Diomedes, who is frequently known by the patronymic Tydides.

Q250588.label: Astraeus
Q250588.description: Greek astrological god associated with winds
Q250588.lead: In Greek mythology, Astraeus or Astraios is the son of Crius and Eurybia and the consort of Eos (goddess of the dawn). He is said to be the father of the winds.

Q252387.label: Palamedes
Q252387.lead: Palamedes was a Euboean prince, son of King Nauplius in Greek mythology. He joined the rest of the Greeks in the expedition against Troy.

Q25393.label: Common Nightingale
Q25393.lead: The common nightingale, rufous nightingale or simply nightingale (Luscinia megarhynchos), is a small passerine bird which is known for its powerful and beautiful song, often described as one of the most beautiful sounds in nature. An Old World flycatcher, it belongs to a group of more terrestrial species, often called chats.

Q2551319.label: Stasinus
Q2551319.lead: Stasinus of Cyprus was a semi-legendary early Greek poet. He is best known for his lost work Cypria, which was one of the poems belonging to the Epic Cycle that narrated the War of Troy.

Q2629041.label: Phylacus
Q2629041.description: mythical son of Deion, eponym of Phylace

Q26296.label: Electryon
Q26296.description: son of Perseus in Greek mythology
Q26296.lead: In Greek mythology, Electryon was a king of Tiryns and Mycenae or Medea in Argolis.

Q2640491.label: Schoeneus
Q2640491.description: father of Atalante in Greek mythology

Q269243.label: Triptolemus
Q269243.description: mythical promulgator of agriculture at Eleusis
Q269243.lead: Triptolemus, also known as Buzyges (Ancient Greek: Βουζύγης, romanized: Bouzýgēs, lit. 'Bull-hitcher'), was a hero of Eleusis in Greek mythology, central to the Eleusinian Mysteries and is worshipped as the inventor and patron of agriculture. Triptolemus is credited with being the first to sow seed for cultivation after being taught by Demeter and is credited for the use of oxen and the plough.

Q270867.label: Terra
Q270867.description: personification of the Earth in ancient Roman religion and mythology
Q270867.lead: In ancient Roman religion and mythology, Tellus, Terra, Tellus Mater or Terra Mater ("Earth" or "Mother Earth") is the personification of the Earth. Although Tellus and Terra are hardly distinguishable during the Imperial era, Tellus was the name of the original earth goddess in the religious practices of the Republic or earlier.

Q2711488.label: Margites
Q2711488.lead: The Margites is a comic mock-epic ascribed to Homer that is largely lost. From references to the work that survived, it is known that its central character is an exceedingly stupid man named Margites (from ancient Greek μάργος, margos, "raving, mad; lustful"), who was so dense he did not know which parent had given birth to him.

Q271809.label: Proclus
Q271809.lead: Proclus Lycius, called Proclus the Successor (Ancient Greek: Πρόκλος ὁ Διάδοχος, Próklos ho Diádokhos), was a Greek Neoplatonic philosopher, one of the last major classical philosophers of late antiquity.

Q272000.label: Deianira
Q272000.description: wife of Heracles in Greek mythology
Q272000.lead: Deianira, Deïanira, or Deianeira, also known as Dejanira, is a Calydonian princess in Greek mythology whose name translates as "man-destroyer" or "destroyer of her husband". She was the wife of Heracles and, in late Classical accounts, his unwitting murderer, killing him with the poisoned Shirt of Nessus.

Q272047.label: Endymion
Q272047.description: son of Aethlius in Greek mythology
Q272047.lead: In Greek mythology, Endymion was variously a handsome Aeolian shepherd, hunter, or king who was said to rule and live at Olympia in Elis. He was also venerated and said to reside on Mount Latmus in Caria, on the west coast of Asia Minor.

Q272918.label: Chronos
Q272918.description: personification of Time in ancient Greek religion
Q272918.lead: Chronos, also spelled Chronus, is a personification of time in Greek mythology, who is also discussed in pre-Socratic philosophy and later literature. His consort is the goddess Ananke.

Q27613.label: Cadmus
Q27613.description: mythological founder of Thebes, son of Agenor
Q27613.lead: In Greek mythology, Cadmus was the legendary founder of Boeotian Thebes. He was, alongside Perseus and Bellerophon, the greatest hero and slayer of monsters before the days of Heracles.

Q278930.label: Epeius
Q278930.description: mythical character, Achean soldier who built the Trojan Horse
Q278930.lead: Epeius or Epeus was a mythological Greek soldier during the Trojan War or, in some accounts, one of the Achaean Leaders, at the head of a contingent of 30 ships from the islands of the Cyclades. He was also the architect of the Wooden Horse, by means of which the Achaeans took Troy; he was himself among those warriors who hid inside it.

Q28045388.label: Antiphus
Q28045388.lead: In Greek mythology, Antiphus or Ántiphos is a name attributed to multiple individuals: Antiphus, a Phthian prince as the son of King Myrmidon and Peisidice, and brother of Actor. He may be the same with Antippus, the father of Hippea who became the mother of Polyphemus, Caeneus and Ischys by Elatus, king of the Lapiths.

Q2827213.label: Agrius
Q2827213.description: mythological son of Odysseus and Circe

Q28362782.label: Lysippe
Q28362782.description: Greek mythological character; daughter of Proetus

Q284487.label: Anaxibia
Q284487.description: sister of Agamemnon and Menelaus, spouse of Strophius, mother of Pylades in Greek mythology

Q296857.label: Mausolus
Q296857.description: Satrap of Caria from 377 BCE to 353 BCE
Q296857.lead: Mausolus was a ruler of Caria (377–353 BCE) and a satrap of the Achaemenid Empire. He enjoyed the status of king or dynast by virtue of the powerful position created by his father Hecatomnus (Carian: 𐊴𐊭𐊪𐊳𐊫 K̂tmño), who was the first satrap of Caria from the hereditary Hecatomnid dynasty.

Q2993260.label: Echemus
Q2993260.description: son of Aeropus in Greek mythology
Q2993260.lead: In Greek mythology, Echemus was the Tegean king of Arcadia who succeeded Lycurgus. His name was derived from the Greek verb ἔχω (echō), meaning "to have, hold, or keep," combined with elements denoting posture or retention.

Q301219.label: Erechtheus
Q301219.lead: Erechtheus in Greek mythology was a king of Athens, the founder of the polis and, in his role as god, attached to Poseidon, as "Poseidon Erechtheus". The name Erichthonius is carried by a son of Erechtheus, but Plutarch conflated the two names in the myth of the begetting of Erechtheus.

Q3043953.label: Makedon
Q3043953.lead: In Greek mythology, Makedon, also spelled Makednos (Μακεδνός) or transcribed Macedon, was the eponymous ancestor of the Makedones according to various ancient Greek fragmentary narratives. In most versions, he appears as a native or immigrant leader from Epirus, who gave his name to Macedonia, previously called Emathia according to Strabo, which according to Marsyas of Pella was until then a part of ancient Thrace.

Q3085116.label: Pandora
Q3085116.lead: In Greek mythology, Pandora was Phthian princess as the daughter of King Deucalion of Thessaly. She was named after her maternal grandmother, the more infamous Pandora.

Q308902.label: Victoria
Q308902.lead: In ancient Roman religion, Victoria or Victory is the deified personification of victory. She first appeared during the first Punic War, seemingly as a Romanised re-naming of Nike, the goddess of victory associated with Rome's Greek allies in the Greek mainland and in Magna Graecia.

Q320660.label: Chrysaor
Q320660.lead: In Greek mythology, Chrysaor was the brother of the winged horse Pegasus, often depicted as a young man, the son of Poseidon and Medusa, born when Perseus decapitated the Gorgon Medusa.

Q321541.label: Meleager
Q321541.description: son of Oeneus in Greek mythology, king of Calydon
Q321541.lead: Meleager was a hero in Greek mythology, venerated in his temenos at Calydon in Aetolia. He was famed as the host of the Calydonian boar hunt in the epic tradition that was reworked by Homer, and was also mentioned as one of the Argonauts.

Q322639.label: Neoptolemus
Q322639.lead: In Greek mythology, Neoptolemus, originally called Pyrrhus at birth (Πύρρος, Pýrrhos, 'red'), was the son of the mythical warrior Achilles and the princess Deidamia, and the brother of Oneiros. He became the progenitor of the ruling dynasty of the Molossians of ancient Epirus.

Q326767.label: Thaumas
Q326767.lead: In Greek mythology, Thaumas or Thaumant was a sea god, son of Pontus and Gaia, and the full brother of Nereus, Phorcys, Ceto and Eurybia.

Q3291388.label: Timandra
Q3291388.description: Greek mythological character, daughter of Leda and Tyndareus
Q3291388.lead: In Greek mythology, Timandra was a Spartan princess and later queen of Arcadia. Her name is derived from two ancient Greek root words: timē (meaning honor or respect) and aner or andros (meaning man).

Q3303321.label: Graecus
Q3303321.description: mythological Greek character; son of Pandora II and Zeus
Q3303321.lead: In Greek mythology, Graecus was the son of Zeus and Pandora, daughter of Deucalion, and the eponym of the Graecians. According to the Byzantine author John the Lydian (c.

Q330584.label: Amphiaraus
Q330584.lead: Amphiaraus or Amphiaraos was in Greek mythology the son of Oicles, a seer, and one of the leaders of the Seven against Thebes. Amphiaraus at first refused to go with Adrastus on this expedition against Thebes as he foresaw the death of everyone who joined the expedition.

Q331327.label: Telamon
Q331327.description: one of the Argonauts of Jason, in Greek mythology
Q331327.lead: Telamon in Greek mythology was the son of King Aeacus of Aegina, and Endeïs, a mountain nymph. The elder brother of Peleus, Telamon sailed alongside Jason as one of his Argonauts, and was present at the hunt for the Calydonian Boar.

Q332324.label: Laomedon
Q332324.lead: In Greek mythology, Laomedon was a Trojan king, son of Ilus and thus nephew of Ganymede and Assaracus. Laomedon was variously identified with different parents and siblings, as well as numerous children, including Priam and Tithonus.

Q3337178.label: Nausithous
Q3337178.description: son of Odysseus in Greek mythology

Q334447.label: Kratos
Q334447.lead: In Greek mythology, Kratos also known as Cratus or Cratos, is the divine personification of strength. He is the son of Pallas and Styx.

Q334787.label: Astyanax
Q334787.lead: In Greek mythology, Astyanax was the son of Hector, the crown prince of Troy, and of his wife, Princess Andromache of Cilician Thebe. His birth name was Scamandrius (in Greek: Σκαμάνδριος Skamandrios, after the river Scamander), but the people of Troy nicknamed him Astyanax (i.e.

Q334817.label: Polynices
Q334817.lead: In Greek mythology, Polynices (also Polyneices) was the son of Oedipus and either Jocasta or Euryganeia, and the brother of Eteocles, Antigone, and Ismene. When Oedipus discovered that he had killed his father and married his mother, he blinded himself and left Thebes, leaving Polynices and Eteocles to rule jointly.

Q336428.label: Hellen
Q336428.lead: In Greek mythology, Hellen is the eponymous progenitor of the Hellenes. He is the son of Deucalion (or Zeus) and Pyrrha, and the father of three sons, Dorus, Xuthus, and Aeolus.

Q3378668.label: Phaethon
Q3378668.description: son of Eos by Cephalus or Tithonus in Greek mythology
Q3378668.lead: In Greek mythology, Phaethon was a son of Eos by Cephalus of Athens or Tithonus, born in Syria.

Q3381352.label: Phocus
Q3381352.description: son of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q3381352.lead: In Greek mythology, Phocus was a Corinthian prince who later became the eponymous ruler of Phocis.

Q34201.label: Zeus
Q34201.description: Greek god of the sky and king of the gods
Q34201.lead: Zeus is the supreme deity of the Greek pantheon. He is a sky and thunder god in ancient Greek religion and mythology, who rules as king of the gods on Mount Olympus.

Q342343.label: Perieres
Q342343.lead: In Greek mythology, Perieres was the 'overbold' king of Messene, an ancient polis in southern Peloponnese.

Q348668.label: Acamas
Q348668.lead: In Greek mythology, Acamas or Akamas was a hero in the Trojan War.

Q35500.label: Aphrodite
Q35500.description: Greek goddess of love, beauty, pleasure, and procreation
Q35500.lead: Aphrodite is an ancient Greek goddess associated with love and beauty. Aphrodite's main cult centers were Cythera, Cyprus, Corinth, and Athens.

Q3567491.label: Galaxaura
Q3567491.lead: In Greek mythology, Galaxaura was the 'lovely' Oceanid, one of the 3,000 water-nymph daughters of the Titans Oceanus and his sister-spouse Tethys. Her name means "calm" or "the charmer" or "like the refreshing coolness of a shady stream".

Q3606203.label: Aphidnus
Q3606203.description: king in Attica in Greek mythology

Q3622209.label: Arete
Q3622209.description: person in Greek mythology, wife of Alcinous
Q3622209.lead: In Greek mythology, Queen Arete of Scheria was the wife of Alcinous and mother of Nausicaa and Laodamas.

Q3635513.label: Passalus
Q3635513.description: son of Oceanus in Greek mythology

Q3667219.label: Chaeron
Q3667219.description: son of Apollo in Greek mythology

Q3680510.label: Cleolia
Q3680510.description: daughter of Dias and wife of Pleisthenes
Q3680510.lead: In Greek mythology, Cleolla or Cleola was the daughter of Dias, the son of Pelops, and by some accounts the mother, or grandmother, of Agamemnon and Menelaus. Most accounts have Agamemnon and Menelaus, as the sons of Atreus, the son of Pelops, and Aerope.

Q368423.label: Stheneboea
Q368423.description: wife of King Proetus in Greek mythology
Q368423.lead: In Greek mythology, Stheneboea also called Antea in Homer (Ancient Greek: Ἄντεια, romanized: Ánteia), is the daughter of Iobates, king in Lycia. She was the queen consort of Proetus, joint-king in the Argolid along with Acrisius, having his seat at Tiryns.

Q3705305.label: Demophon
Q3705305.description: king of Elaeus in Greek mythology
Q3705305.lead: Demophon is a king of Elaeus in Thrace from ancient Greek and Roman mythology. In order to combat a deadly disease that plagued his city, Demophon sacrificed the daughters of noblemen, an act that enraged Mastusius, the father of one of the victims, who then sought revenge.

Q37122.label: Athena
Q37122.description: goddess of wisdom and war in ancient Greek religion and mythology
Q37122.lead: Athena or Athene, often given the epithet Pallas, is an ancient Greek goddess associated with wisdom, warfare, and handicraft who was later syncretised with the Roman goddess Minerva and Etruscan Menrva. Athena was regarded as the patron and protectress of various cities across Greece, particularly the city of Athens, from which she most likely received her name.

Q37340.label: Apollo
Q37340.description: god in Greek and later Roman mythology
Q37340.lead: Apollo is one of the Olympian deities in ancient Greek religion and mythology. His numerous functions include light, healing, prophecy, music, poetry, and archery.

Q3744924.label: Phylas
Q3744924.description: mythological Greek character; son of Antiochus, great-grandson of Phylas king of Ephyra

Q38012.label: Hera
Q38012.description: Greek goddess, wife and sister of Zeus
Q38012.lead: In ancient Greek religion, Hera is the goddess of marriage, women, and family, and the protector of women during childbirth. In Greek mythology, she is queen among the twelve Olympians on Mount Olympus, sister and wife of Zeus, and daughter of the Titans Cronus and Rhea.

Q380832.label: Aello
Q380832.description: one of the Harpy sisters in Greek mythology

Q381459.label: Agave
Q381459.description: daughter of Cadmus in Greek mythology
Q381459.lead: In Greek mythology, Agave, was the daughter of Cadmus and a princess of Thebes. She is most well known for her role in the myths surrounding her nephew, Dionysus, god of wine.

Q381931.label: Aethlius
Q381931.description: son of Zeus in Greek mythology
Q381931.lead: Aethlius or Aithlios or Aethnos was, in Greek mythology, the first king of Elis.

Q3887143.label: Otreus
Q3887143.description: king of Phrygia in Greek mythology
Q3887143.lead: In the Greek mythological tradition, Otreus was the legendary founder of Otrea in southern Bithynia (Hellespont Phrygia). His name has also been linked to Otrous, a Phyrgian town on the Eucarpitic plain.

Q3893378.label: Panopeus
Q3893378.description: son of Phocus in Greek mythology
Q3893378.lead: In Greek mythology, Panopeus was a son of Phocus by Asteria or Asterodia, and twin brother of Crisus. The two brothers were so inimical towards each other that they began fighting while still in their mother's womb, just like Proetus and Acrisius did.

Q3899862.label: Periclymenus
Q3899862.description: son of Neleus in Greek mythology

Q390363.label: Agamedes
Q390363.description: mythical character, builder of temple at Delphi
Q390363.lead: In Greek mythology, Agamedes was a son of Erginus (according to some traditions, the son of Stymphalus and grandson of Arcas).

Q390461.label: Aganus
Q390461.description: son of Paris and Helen of Troy

Q3907369.label: Polypoetes
Q3907369.description: son of Odysseus in Greek mythology

Q391010.label: Chalciope
Q391010.lead: Chalciope, in Greek mythology, was a Colchian princess as the daughter of King Aeëtes. Acusilaus, Hesiod and Hesychius referred to her as Iophossa (Ιoφώσσης) while according to Pherecydes, she was called Euenia (Εύηνίαν).

Q392387.label: Agelaus
Q392387.description: son of Oeneus in Greek mythology

Q392435.label: Aristaeus
Q392435.lead: Aristaeus was the mythological culture hero credited with the discovery of many rural useful arts and handicrafts, including beekeeping. He was the son of the huntress Cyrene and Apollo.

Q392631.label: Agenor
Q392631.description: mythical Phoenician king, father of Cadmus
Q392631.lead: Agenor was in Greek mythology and history a Phoenician king of Tyre or Sidon. The Greek historian Herodotus (c.

Q393261.label: Cyrene
Q393261.description: nymph, mother of Aristaeus by Apollo
Q393261.lead: In Greek mythology, Cyrene, also spelled Kyrene, was the etymon of the Greek colony of Cyrene, Libya. She was said to have been a Thessalian princess and huntress who became the queen regnant of Cyrene, founded and named in her honor by the god Apollo.

Q39503.label: Artemis
Q39503.description: goddess of the hunt and the wild in ancient Greek religion and mythology
Q39503.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Artemis is the goddess of hunting, the wilderness, wild animals, transitions, nature, vegetation, childbirth, care of children, and chastity. She was often said to roam the forests and mountains, attended by an entourage of nymphs.

Q3984506.label: Thero
Q3984506.description: daughter of Phylas and Leipephilene, and sister of Hippotes

Q398524.label: Philyra
Q398524.lead: In Greek mythology, Philyra or Phillyra was one of the 3,000 Oceanids, water-nymph daughters of the Titans Oceanus and Tethys.

Q4024302.label: Zetes
Q4024302.description: son of Boreas in Greek mythology

Q404076.label: Aidos
Q404076.lead: Aidos or Aedos was the Greek personification of either shame or modesty. Aidos, as a quality, was that feeling of reverence or shame which restrains men from wrong.

Q404208.label: Aegaeon
Q404208.description: deity or giant from Greek mythology

Q404844.label: Aegyptus
Q404844.description: son of Belus in Greek mythology
Q404844.lead: In Greek mythology, Aegyptus or Ægyptus was a legendary king of ancient Egypt. He was a descendant of the princess Io through his father Belus, and of the river-god Nilus as both the father of Achiroe, his mother and as a great, great-grandfather on his father's side.

Q4062501.label: Alcyone
Q4062501.description: daughter of Sthenelus in Greek mythology

Q406388.label: Aiolos
Q406388.description: hero ancestor of the Aeolians, son of Hellen
Q406388.lead: In Greek mythology, Aeolus or Aiolos was the son of Hellen, the ruler of Aeolia (later called Thessaly), and the eponym of the Aeolians, one of the four main tribes of the Greeks. According to the mythographer Apollodorus, Aeolus was the father of seven sons: Cretheus, Sisyphus, Athamas, Salmoneus, Deion, Magnes, Perieres, and five daughters: Canace, Alcyone, Pisidice, Calyce, and Perimede.

Q4068355.label: Arabos
Q4068355.description: mythological Greek character, eponym of the Arabs

Q40730.label: Demeter
Q40730.description: Greek goddess of the harvest, grains, and agriculture
Q40730.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Demeter is the Olympian goddess of the harvest and agriculture, presiding over crops, grains, food, and the fertility of the earth. Although Demeter is mostly known as a grain goddess, she also appeared as a goddess of health, birth, and marriage, and had connections to the Underworld.

Q40901.label: Ares
Q40901.description: Greek god of war and combat
Q40901.lead: Ares is the Greek god of war and courage. He is one of the Twelve Olympians, and the son of Zeus and Hera.

Q410082.label: Aeson
Q410082.description: father of Jason in Greek mythology
Q410082.lead: In Greek mythology, Aeson was a king of Iolcus in Thessaly. He was the father of the hero Jason.

Q41054.label: Epimetheus
Q41054.lead: In Greek mythology, Epimetheus is the brother of Prometheus, with the complementary pair serving as archetypal representations of mankind. Both are sons of the Titan Iapetus; while Prometheus ("forethought, or foresight") is portrayed as ingeniously clever, Epimetheus ("afterthought, or hindsight") is considered inept and foolish.

Q41127.label: Poseidon
Q41127.description: one of the twelve Olympians presiding over the sea, storms, earthquakes and horses
Q41127.lead: Poseidon is one of the twelve Olympians in ancient Greek religion and mythology, presiding over the sea, storms, earthquakes and horses. He was the protector of seafarers and the guardian of many Hellenic cities and colonies.

Q41410.label: Hades
Q41410.description: god of the underworld in Greek mythology
Q41410.lead: Hades, in the ancient Greek religion and mythology, is the god of the dead and riches and the King of the underworld, with which his name became synonymous. Hades was the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, although this also made him the last son to be regurgitated by his father.

Q41419.label: Hestia
Q41419.description: Greek goddess of the hearth and the home
Q41419.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Hestia is the virgin goddess of the hearth and the home. In myth, she is the firstborn child of the Titans Cronus and Rhea, and one of the Twelve Olympians.

Q41484.label: Hermes
Q41484.description: Olympian god in Greek religion and mythology; the emissary and messenger of the gods; the god of trade, heraldry, merchants, commerce, roads, thieves, trickery, sports, travelers, and athletes; the son of Zeus and the Pleiad Maia
Q41484.lead: Hermes is an Olympian deity in ancient Greek religion and mythology considered the herald of the gods. He is also widely considered the protector of human heralds, travelers, thieves, merchants, and orators.

Q416384.label: Acastus
Q416384.lead: Acastus is a character in Greek mythology. He sailed with Jason and the Argonauts, and participated in the hunt for the Calydonian Boar.

Q4165042.label: Dolichus
Q4165042.description: character in poetry of Homer and Hesiod

Q41680.label: Dionysus
Q41680.description: ancient Greek god of winemaking and wine
Q41680.lead: In ancient Greek religion and myth, Dionysus is the god of wine-making, orchards, fruit, vegetation, fertility, festivity, insanity, ritual madness, religious ecstasy, and theatre. He was also known as Bacchus (Ancient Greek: Βάκχος Bacchos) by the Greeks (a name later adopted by the Romans) for a frenzy he is said to induce called baccheia.

Q41746.label: Achilles
Q41746.description: Greek mythological hero of the Trojan War
Q41746.lead: In Greek mythology, Achilles or Achilleus (Ancient Greek: Ἀχιλλεύς, romanized: Achilleús) was a hero of the Trojan War who was known as being the greatest of all the Greek warriors. The central character in Homer's Iliad, he was the son of the Nereid Thetis and Peleus, king of Phthia and famous Argonaut.

Q420269.label: Arges
Q420269.lead: Arges was one of the three Hesiodic Cyclopes in Greek mythology. He was elsewhere called Acmonides or Pyracmon.

Q4218933.label: Ceyx
Q4218933.lead: In Greek mythology, Ceyx was a king of Trachis in Thessaly.

Q4233220.label: master
Q4233220.description: historic term for a ship's officer
Q4233220.lead: The master, or sailing master, is an historical rank for a naval warrant officer trained in and responsible for the navigation and ship handling of a sailing vessel. In the Royal Navy, the master was ranked with, but after, the lieutenants.

Q423894.label: Acusilaus
Q423894.lead: Acusilaus, Acusilas, Acousileos, or Akousilaos of Argos, son of Cabas or Scabras, was a Greek logographer and mythographer who lived in the latter half of the 6th century BC but whose work survives only in fragments and summaries of individual points. He is one of the authors (= FGrHist 2) whose fragments were collected in Felix Jacoby's Die Fragmente der griechischen Historiker.

Q4300425.label: Molione
Q4300425.description: Mythological character, mother of the Moliones
Q4300425.lead: In Greek mythology, Molione or Moline (Μολίνη) was a member of the Aetolian royal family.

Q431387.label: Deidamia
Q431387.description: Greek mythological figure, daughter of Lycomedes
Q431387.lead: In Greek mythology, Deidamia is a daughter of King Lycomedes, who lives on the island of Scyros. She marries Achilles, by whom she becomes the mother of Neoptolemus.

Q43182.label: Eratosthenes
Q43182.description: Greek mathematician, geographer, poet, astronomer, librarian and music theorist
Q43182.lead: Eratosthenes of Cyrene was an Ancient Greek polymath: a philosopher, scholar, mathematician, geographer, poet, astronomer, and music theorist.

Q43353.label: Aristophanes
Q43353.description: Classical Athenian comic playwright (c. 446 – c. 386 BC)
Q43353.lead: Aristophanes was an Ancient Greek comic playwright from Athens. He wrote forty plays, of which eleven survive virtually complete.

Q440440.label: Althaea
Q440440.lead: In Greek mythology, Althaea, also rendered Althea or Althaia, was queen of Calydon through her marriage to King Oeneus. Althaea appears in myths surrounding the fabled Calydonian boar hunt, and is infamous for murdering her son Meleager.

Q44204.label: Cronus
Q44204.description: ruler of the Titans in Greek mythology
Q44204.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Cronus, Cronos, or Kronos was the leader and youngest of the Titans, the children of Gaia (Earth) and Uranus (Sky). Cronus castrated and overthrew his father and then ruled during the mythological Golden Age until he himself was overthrown by his son, Zeus, and imprisoned in Tartarus.

Q44233.label: Hesiod
Q44233.description: ancient Greek poet of the archaic period
Q44233.lead: Hesiod was an Ancient Greek poet generally thought to have been active between 750 and 650 BC, around the same time as Homer.

Q44384.label: Hephaestus
Q44384.lead: Hephaestus is the Greek god of artisans, blacksmiths, carpenters, craftsmen, fire, metallurgy, metalworking, sculpture, and volcanoes. In Greek mythology, Hephaestus was the son of Hera, either on her own or by her husband Zeus.

Q4439972.label: Aglaea
Q4439972.description: one of the Graces (Charites) in Greek mythology
Q4439972.lead: In Greek mythology, Aglaia, Aglaïa or Aglaea is a goddess, one of the Charites (known as the Graces in Roman mythology). She is the goddess of splendor, brilliance and brightness.

Q444459.label: Alcidamas
Q444459.description: 4th century BC Greek sophist and rhetorician
Q444459.lead: Alcidamas, of Elaea, in Aeolis, was a Greek sophist and rhetorician, who flourished in the 4th century BC.

Q45713.label: titan
Q45713.description: members of the second order of divine beings in Greek mythology
Q45713.lead: In Greek mythology, the Titans were the deities who preceded the Olympians. According to the Theogony of Hesiod, they were the twelve children of the primordial deities Uranus (Sky) and Gaia (Earth).

Q457294.label: Pallas
Q457294.lead: In Greek mythology, Pallas or Pallantes was the son of the Titans Crius and Eurybia, the brother of Astraeus and Perses, the husband of Styx, and the father of Zelus, Nike, Kratos, and Bia. Hyginus says that Pallas, whom he calls "the giant", also fathered with Styx: Scylla, Fontus ("Fountains") and Lacus ("Lakes").

Q45967.label: Persephone
Q45967.description: Greek goddess of the seasons and the queen of the underworld; married with Hades
Q45967.lead: In ancient Greek mythology and religion, Persephone is the daughter of Zeus and Demeter. She became the queen of the underworld after her abduction by her uncle Hades, the king of the underworld, who later took her into marriage.

Q461212.label: Dardanus
Q461212.description: mythological Greek character, son of Zeus
Q461212.lead: In Greek mythology, Dardanus was the founder of the city of Dardanus at the foot of Mount Ida in the Troad. Dardanus, a son of Zeus and the Pleiad Electra, was a significant figure in Greek mythology.

Q463107.label: Autolycus
Q463107.description: son of Daedalion in Greek mythology
Q463107.lead: In Greek mythology, Autolycus was a robber who had the power to metamorphose or make invisible the things he stole. He had his residence on Mount Parnassus and was renowned among men for his cunning and oaths.

Q465331.label: Ionians
Q465331.lead: The Ionians were one of the four major tribes that the Greeks considered themselves to be divided into during the ancient period; the other three being the Dorians, Aeolians, and Achaeans. The Ionian dialect was one of the three major linguistic divisions of the Hellenic world, together with the Dorian and Aeolian dialects.

Q4668463.label: Acaste
Q4668463.lead: In Greek mythology, Acaste was one of the 3,000 Oceanids, the daughters of the Titans Oceanus and his sister-spouse Tethys. According to the Homeric Hymn 2 to Demeter, Acaste was, along with several of her Oceanid sisters, one of the companions of Persephone who were picking flowers with her when she was abducted by Hades.

Q467515.label: Zephyrus
Q467515.description: Greek god of the wind from the west, spring, fertility, procreation, luck, rebirth, vegetation, flowers, bees and honey
Q467515.lead: In Greek mythology and religion, Zephyrus, also spelled in English as Zephyr, is the god and personification of the West wind, one of the several wind gods, the Anemoi. The son of Eos (the goddess of the dawn) and Astraeus, Zephyrus is the most gentle and favourable of the winds, associated with flowers, springtime and even procreation.

Q4679171.label: Admete
Q4679171.lead: In Greek mythology, Admete was one of the 3,000 Oceanids, daughters of the Titans Oceanus and his sister-wife Tethys. The name of Admete/ Admeta was the female form of Admetus.

Q4687914.label: Alphesiboea
Q4687914.description: character in Greek mythology, mother of Adonis (according to some versions of the myth)

Q47231.label: Odysseus
Q47231.lead: In Greek and Roman mythology, Odysseus, also known by the Latin variant Ulysses (UK also ; Latin: Ulysses, Ulixes), is a legendary Greek king of Ithaca and the hero of Homer's epic poem, the Odyssey. Odysseus also plays a key role in Homer's Iliad and other works in that same epic cycle.

Q474822.label: Amphidamas
Q474822.lead: Amphidamas[(/æmˈfɪdəməs/] was the name of a historical king of Chalcis, who died about 730 BC after the Lelantine War; whose burial ceremony is associated with the poetic agon is mentioned by Hesiod.

Q474888.label: Amphilochus
Q474888.lead: In Greek mythology, Amphilochus was an Argive hero and one of the Epigoni.

Q482134.label: Amythaon
Q482134.description: son of Cretheus in Greek mythology
Q482134.lead: In Greek mythology, Amythaon is the son of Cretheus, the king of Iolcus.

Q48961.label: Calypso
Q48961.lead: In Greek mythology, Calypso was a nymph who lived on the island of Ogygia, where, according to Homer's Odyssey, she detained Odysseus for seven years against his will. She promised Odysseus immortality if he would stay with her, but Odysseus preferred to return home.

Q494886.label: Pylades
Q494886.lead: In Greek mythology, Pylades was a Phocian prince as the son of King Strophius and Anaxibia, the daughter of Atreus and sister of Agamemnon and Menelaus. He is mostly known for his relationship with his cousin Orestes, son of Agamemnon.

Q496595.label: Alcinous
Q496595.description: mythical character, King of the Phaeacians, son of Nausithous and brother of Rhexenor
Q496595.lead: In Greek mythology, Alcinous was a son of Nausithous and brother of Rhexenor. After the latter's death, he married his brother's daughter Arete who bore him Nausicaa, Halius, Clytoneus and Laodamas.

Q501667.label: Lycaon
Q501667.description: Greek mythical character, king of Arcadia, son of Pelasgus and Meliboea
Q501667.lead: In Greek mythology, Lycaon was a king of Arcadia who, in the most popular version of the myth, killed and cooked his son Nyctimus and served him to Zeus, to see whether the god was sufficiently all-knowing to recognize human flesh. Disgusted, Zeus transformed Lycaon into a wolf, while Nyctimus was restored to life.

Q504076.label: Iolaos
Q504076.description: nephew of Heracles in Greek mythology
Q504076.lead: In Greek mythology, Iolaus was a Theban divine hero. He was famed for being Heracles's charioteer and squire, and for helping with some of his Labors, as well as for being one of the Argonauts.

Q506285.label: Eurybia
Q506285.lead: In Greek mythology, Eurybia, described as "[having] a heart of flint within her", was the daughter of Pontus and Gaia, consort to the Titan Crius, and mother of Astraeus, Perses, and Pallas. An older, relatively minor deity, her role in most mythology is as the ancestor of other gods, and she often plays no role in the mythology.

Q506550.label: Eteocles
Q506550.lead: In Greek mythology, Eteocles was a king of Thebes, the son of Oedipus and either Jocasta or Euryganeia. Oedipus killed his father Laius and married his mother without knowing his relationship to either.

Q506781.label: Memnon
Q506781.description: mythical Ethiopian king, son of Tithonus and Eos
Q506781.lead: In Greek mythology, Memnon was a king of Aethiopia and son of Tithonus and Eos. During the Trojan War, he brought an army to Troy's defense and killed Antilochus, Nestor's son, during a fierce battle.

Q508543.label: Aerope
Q508543.description: daughter of Catreus, the king of Crete
Q508543.lead: In Greek mythology, Aerope was a Cretan princess as the daughter of Catreus, king of Crete. She was the sister of Clymene, Apemosyne and Althaemenes.

Q50946651.label: Telphusa
Q50946651.description: Greek nymph of a Boeotian spring

Q514746.label: Xuthus
Q514746.lead: In Greek mythology, Xuthus was a Phthian prince who later became a king of Peloponnesus. He was the founder (through his sons) of the Achaean and Ionian nations.

Q5283761.label: Dius
Q5283761.lead: In Greek mythology and history, the name Dius may refer to the following:

Q53606.label: Philammon
Q53606.description: musician son of Apollo in Greek mythology
Q53606.lead: In Greek mythology, Philammon was an excellent musician, a talent he received from his father, Apollo.

Q542758.label: Styx
Q542758.description: Greek divinity of the river Styx
Q542758.lead: In Greek mythology, Styx, also called the River Styx, is a goddess and one of the rivers of the Greek Underworld.

Q5623747.label: Psamathe
Q5623747.lead: In Greek mythology, Psamathe is a Nereid, one of the fifty daughters of the sea god Nereus and the Oceanid Doris. By Aeacus, the king of Aegina, she is the mother of a son, Phocus.

Q570434.label: Idomeneus
Q570434.description: Greek mythical character, King of Crete
Q570434.lead: In Greek mythology, Idomeneus was a Cretan king and commander who led the Cretan armies to the Trojan War, in eighty black ships. He was also one of the suitors of Helen, as well as a comrade of the Telamonian Ajax.

Q577245.label: Cycnus
Q577245.description: character in Greek mythology, son of Ares, killed by Heracles
Q577245.lead: In Greek mythology, Cycnus or Cygnus was a bloodthirsty and cruel man who dwelt either in Pagasae, Thessaly or by the river Echedorus in Macedonia.

Q577552.label: Antilochus
Q577552.lead: In Greek mythology, Antilochus was a prince of Pylos and one of the Achaeans in the Trojan War. He was the youngest prince to command troops.

Q578378.label: Aphareus
Q578378.description: Greek mythological character, son of Perieres
Q578378.lead: In Greek mythology, Aphareus was a Messenian king.

Q580862.label: Antiope
Q580862.description: Greek mythological figure: Amazon, daughter of Ares, wife of Theseus
Q580862.lead: In Greek mythology, Antiope was an Amazon, daughter of Ares and sister to Melanippe, Hippolyta, Penthesilea and possibly Orithyia, queens of the Amazons. Two sisters, Orithyia and Antiope, co-ruled the Amazons.

Q5986347.label: Ichnaea
Q5986347.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, Ichnaea, is an epithet that could be applied to Themis, as in the Homeric Hymn to Delian Apollo, or to Nemesis, who was venerated at Ichnae, a Greek city in Macedon. One Hellenistic source presented her as an independent figure, a daughter of Helios.

Q599482.label: Tros
Q599482.description: ruler of Troy in Greek mythology
Q599482.lead: In Greek mythology, Tros was the founder of the kingdom of Troy, of which the city of Ilios, founded by his son Ilus took the same name, and the son of Erichthonius by Astyoche (daughter of the river god Simoeis) or of Ilus I, from whom he inherited the throne. Tros was the father of three sons: Ilus, Assaracus and Ganymede and two daughters, Cleopatra and Cleomestra.

Q602258.label: Melampus
Q602258.lead: In Greek mythology, Melampus was a legendary soothsayer and healer, originally of Pylos, who ruled at Argos. Melampus was the introducer of the worship of Dionysus, according to Herodotus, who asserted that his powers as a seer were derived from the Egyptians and that he could understand the language of animals.

Q606422.label: Arcas
Q606422.description: son of Callisto in Greek mythology
Q606422.lead: In Greek mythology, Arcas was a hunter who became king of Arcadia. He was remembered for having taught people the arts of weaving and baking bread and for spreading agriculture to Arcadia.

Q6072426.label: Periboea
Q6072426.description: daughter of Hipponous in Greek mythology

Q611124.label: Chryseis
Q611124.description: mythological Greek character, daughter of Chryses in the Iliad
Q611124.lead: Chryseis is a Trojan woman in Homer's Iliad, the daughter of Chryses. Chryseis, her apparent name in the Iliad, means simply "Chryses' daughter"; later writers give her real name as Astynome (Ἀστυνόμη).

Q617160.label: Aegle
Q617160.description: Greek mythological character, daughter of Panopeus

Q617753.label: Belus
Q617753.description: son of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q617753.lead: In Greek mythology, Belus was a king of Egypt and father of Aegyptus and Danaus and (usually) brother to Agenor. The wife of Belus has been named as Achiroe or Side (eponym of the Phoenician city of Sidon).

Q622809.label: Pyrrha
Q622809.description: daughter of Epimetheus and Pandora in Greek mythology
Q622809.lead: In Greek mythology, Pyrrha is the daughter of Epimetheus and Pandora, or of Prometheus.

Q624551.label: Nephele
Q624551.description: cloud goddess, wife of Athamas and mother of Phrixus and Helle
Q624551.lead: In Greek and Roman mythology, Nephele called Nebula by Latin authors, is the name of two figures associated with clouds, who figure respectively in the stories of Ixion and in the story of Phrixus and his sister Helle.

Q637955.label: Neleus
Q637955.description: mythical son of Poseidon or Cretheus and father of Nestor
Q637955.lead: Neleus was a mythological king of Pylos. In some accounts, he was also counted as an Argonaut instead of his son, Nestor.

Q638578.label: Helle
Q638578.lead: Helle, sometimes also called Athamantis (Ancient Greek: Ἀθαμαντίς, "daughter of Athamas"), was a character in Greek mythology who figured prominently in the story of Jason and the Argonauts. Helle is known for giving her name to the strait of Hellespont ("sea of Helle"), into which she fell while crossing it on the back of a flying golden ram with her brother Phrixus—the same flying ram from which the Golden Fleece derived.

Q641065.label: Phineus
Q641065.description: son of Agenor in Greek mythology
Q641065.lead: In Greek mythology, Phineus was a king of Salmydessus in Thrace and seer, who appears in accounts of the Argonauts' voyage. Some accounts make him a king in Paphlagonia or in Arcadia.

Q643504.label: Cephalus
Q643504.description: son of Deioneus and beloved of Eos in Greek mythology
Q643504.lead: In Greek mythology, Cephalus or Kephalos was the son of Deion, the ruler of Phocis, and Diomede.

Q644385.label: Argea
Q644385.description: mythological Greek character, daughter of Adrastus and wife of Polynices
Q644385.lead: In Greek mythology, Argia or Argea was a daughter of King Adrastus of Argos, and of Amphithea, daughter of Pronax. She was married to Polynices, the exiled king of Thebes, and bore him three sons: Thersander, Adrastus, and Timeas.

Q644604.label: Proetus
Q644604.lead: In Greek mythology, Proetus, the son of Abas, was a king of Argos and Tiryns.

Q65078665.label: Dryops
Q65078665.lead: In Greek mythology, Dryops Dryops, a king of Oeta. Dryops, a Trojan prince as one of the children of King Priam of Troy.

Q65118729.label: Laestrygon
Q65118729.lead: In Greek mythology, Laestrygon was the son of Poseidon and possibly of Gaia. He was the father of Telepora or Telepatra, wife of Aeolus, keeper of the winds.

Q656881.label: Tiresias
Q656881.lead: In Greek mythology, Tiresias was a blind prophet of Apollo in Thebes, famous for clairvoyance and for being transformed into a woman for seven years. He was the son of the shepherd Everes and the nymph Chariclo.

Q656887.label: Tityos
Q656887.lead: Tityos or Tityus is a giant from Greek mythology. The son of Zeus and the mortal Elara, Tityos tried to rape the goddess Leto, a former lover of Zeus and the mother of the twin gods Artemis and Apollo.

Q658523.label: Hermione
Q658523.description: daughter of Menelaus and Helen of Troy
Q658523.lead: In Greek mythology, Hermione was the daughter of Menelaus, king of Sparta, and his wife, Helen of Troy. Prior to the Trojan War, Hermione had been betrothed by Tyndareus, her grandfather, to her cousin Orestes, son of her uncle, Agamemnon.

Q66016.label: Muse
Q66016.description: goddess of the inspiration of literature, science and the arts
Q66016.lead: In ancient Greek religion and mythology, the Muses were the inspirational goddesses of literature, science, and the arts. They were considered the source of the knowledge embodied in the poetry, lyric songs, and myths that were related orally for centuries in ancient Greek culture.

Q662968.label: Plouto
Q662968.lead: In Greek mythology, Pluto or Plouto was, according to the late 8th–early 7th century BC Greek poet Hesiod, and the probably nearly as old Homeric Hymn 2 to Demeter, one of the many Oceanid daughters of Oceanus and Tethys. Hesiod calls her "soft eyed", and the Homeric Hymn has her as one of the "deep-bosomed daughters of Oceanus" who were the playmates of Persephone when she was abducted by Hades.

Q663792.label: Sinon
Q663792.description: son of Aesimus in Greek mythology
Q663792.lead: In Greek mythology, Sinon or Sinopos was a Greek warrior during the Trojan War. He is not mentioned by Homer, but his story as given in Virgil's Aeneid and other accounts presents him as a treacherous agent of the Greeks who misleads the Trojans and encourages them to bring the Trojan Horse inside the city.

Q668054.label: Talaus
Q668054.description: son of Bias in Greek mythology
Q668054.lead: In Greek mythology, Talaus was the king of Argos and one of the Argonauts. He was the son of Bias (or Perialces) and Pero, and brother of Arëius and Leodocus.

Q6691.label: Homer
Q6691.description: reputed author of the Iliad and the Odyssey
Q6691.lead: Homer was an ancient Greek poet who is traditionally credited as the author of the Iliad and the Odyssey, two epic poems that are foundational works of ancient Greek literature. Homer was highly revered in ancient Greek society and is considered one of the most influential authors in history.

Q674319.label: Machaon
Q674319.description: character of Greek mythology: son of Asclepius and Coronis, lover of Anticlea; healing hero of the Trojan War; killed by Eurypylus
Q674319.lead: In Greek mythology, Machaon was a son of Asclepius; and the older brother of Podalirius. He and his brother led an army from Tricca in the Trojan War on the side of the Greeks.

Q675699.label: Epaphus
Q675699.description: mythical character, son of Zeus and Io
Q675699.lead: In Greek mythology, Epaphus, also called Apis or Munantius was a son of Zeus and king of Egypt.

Q6762087.label: Mariandynus
Q6762087.description: eponymous hero of the Mariandyni in Greek mythology
Q6762087.lead: In Greek mythology, Mariandynus was the eponymous hero of the Mariandyni tribe in Northern Anatolia. He was an Aeolian, a son of either Cimmerius, or Phrixus, or Phineus (and in the latter case, brother of Thynus).

Q679716.label: Cychreus
Q679716.description: son of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q679716.lead: In Greek mythology, Cychreus was a legendary king of Salamis Island. He was the son of the god Poseidon and the nymph Salamis.

Q6817243.label: Macareus
Q6817243.description: son of Helios and king of Lesbos
Q6817243.lead: In Greek mythology, Macareus or Macar (/ˈmeɪkər/; Μάκαρ Makar) was one of the Heliadae, sons of Helios and Rhodos.

Q682332.label: Nausinous
Q682332.description: character from Greek mythology, son of Odysseus and Calypso
Q682332.lead: In Greek mythology, Nausinous was the son of Odysseus and Calypso. In Theogony by Hesiod, he is said to have a brother named Nausithous.

Q6896910.label: Molurus
Q6896910.lead: In Greek mythology, Molurus was the son of Arisbas. In a surviving fragment of the poem Megalai Ehoiai, Molurus was killed by Hyettus of Argos when Hyettus caught him with his wife.

Q725286.label: Coronis
Q725286.description: goddess from Greek mythology: princess, daughter of Phlegyas, lover of Ischys and Apollo, mother of Asclepius; killed by Apollon and Artemis
Q725286.lead: In Greek mythology, Coronis is a Thessalian princess and a lover of the god Apollo. She was the daughter of Cleophema and Phlegyas, king of the Lapiths.

Q725527.label: Calchas
Q725527.lead: Calchas is an Argive mantis, or seer, in Greek mythology. Calchas appears in the opening scenes of the Iliad and also has a long literary history after Homer.

Q726279.label: Doris
Q726279.lead: Doris, in Greek mythology, was a sea goddess. She was one of the 3,000 Oceanids, daughters of the Titans Oceanus and Tethys.

Q729332.label: Helenus
Q729332.lead: In Greek mythology, Helenus was a gentle and clever seer. He was also a Trojan prince as the son of King Priam and Queen Hecuba of Troy, and the twin brother of the prophetess Cassandra.

Q732066.label: Creon
Q732066.description: king of Thebes in Greek mythology
Q732066.lead: Kreon, also spelled Creon is a figure in Greek mythology best known as the ruler of Thebes in the legend of Oedipus.

Q733985.label: Haemon
Q733985.description: Greek mythical character, son of Creon
Q733985.lead: In Greek mythology, Haemon was the son of Creon and Eurydice, and thus brother of Menoeceus (Megareus), Lycomedes, Megara, Pyrrha and Henioche. The various sources of his myth present differing and contradictory versions of his story.

Q736813.label: Deiphobus
Q736813.description: mythical character, son of Priam of Troy
Q736813.lead: In Greek mythology, Deiphobus was a son of Priam and Hecuba. He was a prince of Troy, and the greatest of Priam's sons after Hector.

Q737306.label: Tithonus
Q737306.description: prince of Troy loved by Eos in Greek mythology
Q737306.lead: In Greek mythology, Tithonus was the lover of Eos, Goddess of the Dawn. He was a prince of Troy, the son of King Laomedon by the Naiad Strymo (Στρυμώ).

Q74055.label: Asbolus
Q74055.lead: In Greek mythology, Asbolus was a centaur. He was a seer and Hesiod calls him an augur (oionistes οἰωνιστής) who read omens in the flight of birds.

Q743482.label: Phrixus
Q743482.description: son of Athamas in Greek mythology
Q743482.lead: In Greek mythology Phrixus was the son of Athamas, king of Boeotia, and Nephele (a goddess of clouds). He was the older brother of Helle and the father of Argus, Phrontis, Melas and Cytisorus by Chalciope (Iophassa), daughter of Aeetes, king of Colchis.

Q744147.label: Iole
Q744147.lead: In Greek mythology, Iole was the daughter of King Eurytus of Oechalia. According to the brief epitome in the Bibliotheca, Eurytus had a beautiful young daughter named Iole who was eligible for marriage.

Q749123.label: Euphemus
Q749123.description: son of Poseidon in Greek mythology
Q749123.lead: In Greek mythology, Euphemus was counted among the Calydonian hunters and the Argonauts, and was connected with the legend of the foundation of Cyrene.

Q749966.label: Oeneus
Q749966.lead: In Greek mythology, Oeneus was a Calydonian king. He was the first who received a vine-plant from Dionysos.

Q750236.label: Polyxena
Q750236.lead: In Greek mythology, Polyxena was the youngest daughter of King Priam of Troy and his queen, Hecuba. She does not appear in Homer, but in several other classical authors, though the details of her story vary considerably.

Q752184.label: Meliae
Q752184.description: ancient Greek mythological nymphs of the ash tree
Q752184.lead: In Greek mythology, the Meliae (also called Meliads) were usually considered to be the nymphs of the ash tree, whose name they shared.

Q753294.label: Atropos
Q753294.description: one of the Fates of Greek Mythology
Q753294.lead: Atropos, in Greek mythology, was the third of the Three Fates or Moirai, goddesses of fate and destiny. Her Roman equivalent was Morta.

Q760213.label: Auge
Q760213.description: daughter of Aleus in Greek mythology
Q760213.lead: In Greek mythology, Auge, was the daughter of Aleus the king of Tegea in Arcadia, and the virgin priestess of Athena Alea. She was also the mother of the hero Telephus by Heracles.

Q771241.label: Polydectes
Q771241.lead: In Greek mythology, King Polydectes is a king of the island of Seriphos in the Cyclades. Polydectes was the ruler of the island when the Argive princess Danaë and her infant son Perseus washed ashore, having been cast away into the sea by Danaë's father Acrisius, who was afraid that his daughter's son would kill him.

Q776139.label: Semele
Q776139.description: mother of Dionysus in Greek mythology
Q776139.lead: In Greek mythology, Semele, or Thyone (Ancient Greek: Θυώνη, romanized: Thyṓnē), was the youngest daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia, and the mother of Dionysus by Zeus (her own great-grandfather). Certain elements of the cult of Dionysus and Semele came from the Phrygians.

Q779406.label: Latinus
Q779406.description: king in Greek and Roman mythology
Q779406.lead: Latinus was a figure both in Greek and Roman mythology. He is often associated with the heroes of the Trojan War, namely Odysseus and Aeneas.

Q781867.label: Menestheus
Q781867.lead: In Greek mythology, Menestheus was a legendary king of Athens during the Trojan War. He was set up as king by the twins Castor and Pollux when Theseus travelled to the Underworld after abducting their sister, Helen, and exiled Theseus from the city after his return.

Q791446.label: Battus
Q791446.lead: Battus was a figure in Greek mythology who witnessed Hermes stealing Apollo's cattle in Maenalus in Arcadia. Hermes gave him a heifer on condition Battus kept the theft secret.

Q8140979.label: Menoetius
Q8140979.lead: Menoetius or Menoetes was a name that refers to three distinct persons from Greek mythology: Menoetius, a second generation Titan, son of Iapetus and Clymene or Asia, and a brother of Atlas, Prometheus and Epimetheus. Menoetius was killed by Zeus with a flash of lightning in the Titanomachy, and banished to Tartarus.

Q82732.label: Aeneas
Q82732.description: Trojan hero, son of Anchises and Aphrodite
Q82732.lead: Aeneas was a Trojan hero in Greco-Roman mythology, the son of the Trojan prince Anchises and the Greek goddess Aphrodite (equivalent to the Roman Venus). His father was a first cousin of King Priam of Troy (both being great-grandsons of Tros, founder of Troy), making Aeneas a second cousin to Priam's children (such as Hector and Paris).

Q829669.label: Clotho
Q829669.description: one of the Fates of Greek mythology
Q829669.lead: Clotho or Klotho is a mythological figure. She was one of the Three Fates or Moirai.

Q831583.label: Phlegyas
Q831583.description: king of the Lapiths in Greek mythology
Q831583.lead: In Greek mythology, Phlegyas was a king of the Lapiths (or the Phlegyans).

Q831589.label: Dactyls
Q831589.description: archaic mythical race of male beings associated with Rhea, the Great Mother
Q831589.lead: In Greek mythology, the Dactyls or Daktyloi were the archaic mythical race of male beings associated with the Great Mother, whether as Cybele or Rhea. Their numbers vary, but often they were ten spirit-men so like the three Korybantes or the Cabeiri that they were often interchangeable.

Q83160.label: Prometheus
Q83160.description: Titan, culture hero, and trickster figure in Greek mythology who defied the gods; son of Iapetus
Q83160.lead: In Greek mythology, Prometheus is a Titan who is responsible for creating and aiding humanity in its earliest days. He defied the Olympian gods by stealing fire from them and giving it to humanity.

Q83223.label: Asclepius
Q83223.lead: Asclepius is a hero and god of medicine in ancient Greek religion and mythology. He is the son of Apollo and Coronis, or Arsinoe, or of Apollo alone.

Q833806.label: Capaneus
Q833806.description: son of Hipponous in Greek mythology
Q833806.lead: In Greek mythology, Capaneus was a son of Hipponous and either Astynome (daughter of Talaus) or Laodice (daughter of Iphis), and husband of Evadne, with whom he fathered Sthenelus. Some call his wife Ianeira.

Q836792.label: Klymene
Q836792.lead: In Greek mythology, Clymene or Klymene is the name of one of the three thousand Oceanid nymphs, usually the wife of Iapetus and mother by him of Prometheus, Epimetheus, Atlas and Menoetius.

Q842435.label: Arion
Q842435.lead: In Greek mythology, Arion or Areion, is a divinely-bred, fabulously fast, black-maned horse. He saved the life of Adrastus, king of Argos, during the war of the Seven against Thebes.

Q845112.label: Enceladus
Q845112.lead: In Greek mythology, Enceladus was one of the Giants, the offspring of Gaia (Earth) and Uranus (Sky). Enceladus was the traditional opponent of Athena during the Gigantomachy, the war between the Giants and the gods, and was said to be buried under Mount Etna in Sicily.

Q846664.label: hawk
Q846664.description: predatory bird of the family Accipitridae
Q846664.lead: Hawks are birds of prey of the family Accipitridae. They are very widely distributed and are found on all continents, except Antarctica.

Q847268.label: Hyllus
Q847268.description: son of Heracles and Deianira in Greek mythology
Q847268.lead: In Greek mythology, Hyllus or Hyllas (Ὕλλᾱς, Hyllas) was a son of Heracles and Deianira and the husband of Iole.

Q847890.label: Oenomaus
Q847890.description: father of Hippodamia; son of Ares
Q847890.lead: In Greek mythology, King Oenomaus of Pisa, was the father of Hippodamia and the son of Ares. His name Oinomaos denotes a wine man.

Q849438.label: Iasion
Q849438.lead: In Greek mythology, Iasion or Iasus (Ancient Greek: Ἴασος, romanized: Íasos), also called Eetion (Ancient Greek: Ἠετίων, romanized: Ēetíōn), was the founder of the mystic rites on the island of Samothrace.

Q849647.label: Briareus
Q849647.lead: In Greek mythology, the Hecatoncheires, also called Hundred-Handers or Centimanes (Latin: Centimani), were three monstrous giants, of enormous size and strength, each with fifty heads and one hundred arms. They were individually named Cottus (the furious), Briareus (or Aegaeon, the sea goat) and Gyges (or Gyes, the long-limbed).

Q867342.label: Troilus
Q867342.description: mythical prince of Troy in Greek mythology
Q867342.lead: Troilus is a legendary character associated with the story of the Trojan War. The first surviving reference to him is in Homer's Iliad, composed in the late 8th century BC. In Greek mythology, Troilus is a young Trojan prince, one of the sons of King Priam (or Apollo) and Hecuba.

Q86805.label: Geryon
Q86805.description: mythical king of far western Mediterranean
Q86805.lead: In Greek mythology, Geryon was a fearsome giant who dwelt on the island Erytheia of the mythic Hesperides in the far west of the Mediterranean. A more literal-minded later generation of Greeks associated the region with Tartessos in southern Iberia.

Q869665.label: Cretheus
Q869665.description: in Greek mythology, king and founder of Iolcus

Q871361.label: Protesilaus
Q871361.lead: In Greek mythology, Protesilaus was a hero in the Iliad who was venerated at cult sites in Thessaly and Thrace. Protesilaus was the son of Iphiclus, a "lord of many sheep"; as grandson of the eponymous Phylacos, he was the leader of the Phylaceans.

Q8860.label: Orion
Q8860.lead: Orion is a prominent set of stars visible during winter in the northern celestial hemisphere. It is one of the 88 modern constellations; it was among the 48 constellations listed by the 2nd-century AD astronomer Ptolemy.

Q898947.label: Lachesis
Q898947.description: one of the Fates of Greek Mythology
Q898947.lead: Lachesis, in ancient Greek religion, was the middle of the Three Fates, or Moirai, alongside her sisters Clotho and Atropos. Normally seen clothed in white, Lachesis is the measurer of the thread spun on Clotho's spindle, and in some texts, determines Destiny.

Q903273.label: Notus
Q903273.description: god of the south wind, storms of late summer and early autumn, wetness, mist, energy, radiance, dryness, freshness, activity, youth and rain in Greek mythology
Q903273.lead: In Greek mythology and religion, Notus is the god of the south wind and one of the Anemoi (wind-gods), sons of the dawn goddess Eos and the star-god Astraeus. A desiccating wind of heat, Notus was associated with the storms of late summer and early autumn, wetness, mist, and was seen as a rain-bringer.

Q905409.label: Dictys
Q905409.description: mythic character, fisherman and brother of King Polydectes
Q905409.lead: Dictys was a name attributed to four men in Greek mythology. Dictys, a fisherman and brother of King Polydectes of Seriphos, both being the sons of Magnes and a Naiad, or of Peristhenes and Androthoe, or else of Poseidon and Cerebia.

Q913161.label: Callirhoe
Q913161.lead: In Greek mythology, Callirhoe (or Kallirhoe, Callirrhoe) was one of the Oceanids, daughters of the Titans: Oceanus and Tethys.

Q9160370.label: Arsinoe
Q9160370.description: daughter of Leucippus, mother of Asclepius

Q916442.label: Telephus
Q916442.lead: In Greek mythology, Telephus was the son of Heracles and Auge, who was the daughter of king Aleus of Tegea. He was adopted by Teuthras, the king of Mysia, in Asia Minor, whom he succeeded as king.

Q917417.label: Merope
Q917417.description: daughter of Oenopion in Greek mythology
Q917417.lead: Merope was a mortal princess in Greek mythology, who was loved by the hunter Orion and was his fiancée. She is called Haero by Parthenius of Nicaea.

Q917719.label: Sarpedon
Q917719.description: Greek mythology character, son of Zeus and Europa

Q922942.label: Pleiades
Q922942.lead: The Pleiades were the seven sister-nymphs, companions of Artemis, the goddess of the hunt. Together with their sisters, the Hyades, they were sometimes called the Atlantides, Dodonides, or Nysiades, nursemaids and teachers of the infant Dionysus.

Q9348775.label: Silens
Q9348775.description: satyr-like semi-divine followers of Dionysus in Greek mythology

Q937216.label: Oenopion
Q937216.description: mythical character, son of Ariadne with Dionysus or Theseus
Q937216.lead: In Greek mythology, Oenopion was a legendary king of Chios, and was said to have brought winemaking to the island, which was assigned to him by Rhadamanthys.

Q939149.label: Eurytus
Q939149.lead: Eurytus of Oechalia (Οἰχαλίᾱ, Oikhalíā), Thessaly, was a skillful archer of Greek mythology who was even said to have instructed Heracles in the art of using the bow.

Q94066.label: Eileithyia
Q94066.description: Greek goddess of childbirth and midwifery
Q94066.lead: Eileithyia or Ilithyia was the Greek goddess of childbirth and midwifery, and the daughter of Zeus and Hera. In the cave of Amnisos (Crete) she was related with the annual birth of the divine child, and her cult is connected with Enesidaon (the earth shaker), who was the chthonic aspect of the god Poseidon.

Q94072.label: Autonoë
Q94072.lead: In Greek mythology, Autonoë was a Theban princess as the eldest daughter of Cadmus, founder of Thebes in Boeotia, and the goddess Harmonia. She was the wife of Aristaeus and mother of Actaeon and possibly Macris.

Q978079.label: Harmonia
Q978079.description: ancient Greek goddess of harmony and concord, spouse of Cadmus; her opposite is Eris
Q978079.lead: In Greek mythology, Harmonia is the goddess of harmony and concord. She is traditionally the daughter of Aphrodite, the goddess of love, and Ares, the god of war.
